claim: Cullin-RING ligases (CRLs) form the major family of E3 ubiquitin ligases.
source: The cullin-RING ligases (CRLs) form the major family of E3 ubiquitin ligases.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the classification of E3 ubiquitin ligases.

claim: The prototypic CRLs in yeast, called SCF enzymes, employ a single E2 enzyme, Cdc34, to build poly-ubiquitin chains required for degradation.
source: The prototypic CRLs in yeast, called SCF enzymes, employ a single E2 enzyme, Cdc34, to build poly-ubiquitin chains required for degradation.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research on yeast SCF function.

claim: Six different human E2 and E3 enzyme activities, including Cdc34 orthologs UBE2R1 and UBE2R2, appear to mediate SCF-catalyzed substrate polyubiquitylation in vitro.
source: In contrast, six different human E2 and E3 enzyme activities, including Cdc34 orthologs UBE2R1 and UBE2R2, appear to mediate SCF-catalyzed substrate polyubiquitylation in vitro.
evidence: This is a summary of prior in vitro experimental findings.

claim: Mass spectrometry was employed to estimate E2 and E3 levels in cells.
source: To enable the quantitative comparisons of SCF-dependent ubiquitylation reactions with physiological enzyme concentrations, mass spectrometry was employed to estimate E2 and E3 levels in cells.
evidence: This describes a method used in the study, with results shown in Table 2.

claim: In combination with UBE2R1/2, the E2 UBE2D3 and the E3 ARIH1 both promoted SCF-mediated polyubiquitylation in a substrate-specific fashion.
source: In combination with UBE2R1/2, the E2 UBE2D3 and the E3 ARIH1 both promoted SCF-mediated polyubiquitylation in a substrate-specific fashion.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the in vitro kinetic experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: UBE2R2 alone had negligible ubiquitylation activity at physiological concentrations.
source: Unexpectedly, UBE2R2 alone had negligible ubiquitylation activity at physiological concentrations and the ablation of UBE2R1/2 had no effect on the stability of SCF substrates in cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5 and Figure 3.

claim: The ablation of UBE2R1/2 had no effect on the stability of SCF substrates in cells.
source: Unexpectedly, UBE2R2 alone had negligible ubiquitylation activity at physiological concentrations and the ablation of UBE2R1/2 had no effect on the stability of SCF substrates in cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: A genome-wide CRISPR screen revealed that an additional E2 enzyme, UBE2G1, buffers against the loss of UBE2R1/2.
source: A genome-wide CRISPR screen revealed that an additional E2 enzyme, UBE2G1, buffers against the loss of UBE2R1/2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the CRISPR screen shown in Figure 6.

claim: UBE2G1 had robust in vitro chain extension activity with SCF.
source: UBE2G1 had robust in vitro chain extension activity with SCF, and UBE2G1 knockdown in cells lacking UBE2R1/2 resulted in stabilization of the SCF substrates p27 and CYCLIN E as well as the CUL2-RING ligase substrate HIF1α.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the in vitro kinetic experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: UBE2G1 knockdown in cells lacking UBE2R1/2 resulted in stabilization of the SCF substrates p27 and CYCLIN E as well as the CUL2-RING ligase substrate HIF1α.
source: UBE2G1 had robust in vitro chain extension activity with SCF, and UBE2G1 knockdown in cells lacking UBE2R1/2 resulted in stabilization of the SCF substrates p27 and CYCLIN E as well as the CUL2-RING ligase substrate HIF1α.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 7a,b.

claim: The human SCF enzyme system is diversified by association with multiple catalytic enzyme partners.
source: The results demonstrate the human SCF enzyme system is diversified by association with multiple catalytic enzyme partners.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: There are at least 600 E3s in the mammalian proteome.
source: There are at least 600 E3s in the mammalian proteome (Deshaies and Joazeiro, 2009), and alterations of the expression levels in several E3s or their substrates have been clinically and biochemically linked to cancer and other diseases in humans (Skaar et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Alterations of the expression levels in several E3s or their substrates have been clinically and biochemically linked to cancer and other diseases in humans.
source: There are at least 600 E3s in the mammalian proteome (Deshaies and Joazeiro, 2009), and alterations of the expression levels in several E3s or their substrates have been clinically and biochemically linked to cancer and other diseases in humans (Skaar et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A chain of at least four ubiquitins is typically required for recognition by the 26S proteasome.
source: A chain of at least four ubiquitins is typically required for recognition by the 26S proteasome (Chau et al., 1989; Thrower, 2000).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The original elucidation of Skp1-cullin-F-box (SCF) ubiquitin ligase function by genetic and biochemical studies in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, suggested that Cdc34 is the only E2 enzyme needed for SCF activity.
source: The original elucidation of Skp1-cullin-F-box (SCF) ubiquitin ligase function by genetic and biochemical studies in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, suggested that Cdc34 is the only E2 enzyme needed for SCF activity (Feldman et al., 1997; Schwob et al., 1994; Skowyra et al., 1997; Verma et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior research.

claim: While the yeast E2s Ubc4/5 do not support SCF activity in vitro, several human SCF ubiquitylation reactions have been reconstituted with the corresponding human E2 orthologs UBE2D1/2/3.
source: While the yeast E2s Ubc4/5 do not support SCF activity in vitro, several human SCF ubiquitylation reactions have been reconstituted with the corresponding human E2 orthologs UBE2D1/2/3 (Sakata et al., 2007; Wu et al., 2003; Wu et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A 'hand-off' model has been proposed where UBE2D3 transfers the first ubiquitin to an SCF-bound substrate, followed by poly-ubiquitin chain elongation catalyzed by the human CDC34 ortholog UBE2R1 or its highly related isoform UBE2R2.
source: A 'hand-off' model has been proposed where UBE2D3 transfers the first ubiquitin to an SCF-bound substrate, followed by poly-ubiquitin chain elongation catalyzed by the human CDC34 ortholog UBE2R1 or its highly related isoform UBE2R2 (Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The E3 enzyme ARIH1 was shown to function with multiple CRLs in a manner similar to UBE2D3 in both humans as well as in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: More recently, the E3 enzyme ARIH1 was shown to function with multiple CRLs in a manner similar to UBE2D3 in both humans (Scott et al., 2016) as well as in Caenorhabditis elegans (Dove et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior research.

claim: UBE2R1/2 are capable of both priming and poly-ubiquitin chain extension on milli-second time scales in in vitro ubiquitylation assays.
source: Despite the apparent requirement for UBE2D1/2/3 or ARIH1 to initiate a poly-ubiquitin chain on human substrates, UBE2R1/2 are capable of both priming and poly-ubiquitin chain extension on milli-second time scales in in vitro ubiquitylation assays (Kleiger et al., 2009b; Pierce et al., 2009; Saha and Deshaies, 2008).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Multi-turnover Michaelis-Menten kinetic assays were used to determine the levels of ARIH1, UBE2D3 and UBE2R2 necessary to saturate either SCFβTRCP or SCFFBW7 complexes.
source: Multi-turnover Michaelis-Menten kinetic assays were used to determine the levels of ARIH1, UBE2D3 and UBE2R2 necessary to saturate either SCFβTRCP or SCFFBW7 complexes (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and Table 1).
evidence: This describes a method used in the study, with results shown in Figure 1 and Table 1.

claim: Single reaction monitoring (SRM) mass spectrometry was used to determine the copy numbers of ARIH1, UBE2D1/2/3, UBE2R1/2, as well as the SCF subunits CUL1 and SKP1 in several common tissue culture cell lines.
source: To address this issue, single reaction monitoring (SRM) mass spectrometry was used to determine the copy numbers of ARIH1, UBE2D1/2/3, UBE2R1/2, as well as the SCF subunits CUL1 and SKP1 in several common tissue culture cell lines, enabling calculation of the protein concentration within the cell (Table 2).
evidence: This describes a method used in the study, with results shown in Table 2.

claim: The rate of chain initiation by ARIH1 was 0.5 sec−1 at saturating concentrations.
source: The rate of chain initiation was 0.5 sec−1, the second ubiquitin transfer to substrate was only modestly slower (0.2 sec−1), and the rate of the third ubiquitin transfer was 0.08 sec−1 (Table 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2 and Table 3.

claim: The second ubiquitin transfer to substrate by ARIH1 was 0.2 sec−1 at saturating concentrations.
source: The rate of chain initiation was 0.5 sec−1, the second ubiquitin transfer to substrate was only modestly slower (0.2 sec−1), and the rate of the third ubiquitin transfer was 0.08 sec−1 (Table 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2 and Table 3.

claim: The rate of the third ubiquitin transfer by ARIH1 was 0.08 sec−1 at saturating concentrations.
source: The rate of chain initiation was 0.5 sec−1, the second ubiquitin transfer to substrate was only modestly slower (0.2 sec−1), and the rate of the third ubiquitin transfer was 0.08 sec−1 (Table 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2 and Table 3.

claim: Reducing the concentration of ARIH1 some 7-fold lower to more physiological levels resulted in only modest changes to the rates of ubiquitin transfer.
source: Reducing the concentration of ARIH1 some 7-fold lower to more physiological levels resulted in only modest changes to the rates of ubiquitin transfer.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2d and Table 3.

claim: At a saturating concentration of 10 μM, the rate of chain initiation by UBE2D3 was 0.1 sec−1 for SCFFBW7 and Cyclin E peptide.
source: At a saturating concentration of 10 μM, the rate of chain initiation was 0.1 sec−1 for SCFFBW7 and Cyclin E peptide (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a,b and Table 3), 5-fold slower than the same rate catalyzed by ARIH1.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Table 3.

claim: When 10 μM UBE2D3 was assayed with β-Catenin peptide and SCFβTRCP, the rate of chain initiation (5 sec−1) was far more rapid than with Cyclin E peptide and SCFFBW7.
source: However, when 10 μM UBE2D3 was assayed with β-Catenin peptide and SCFβTRCP, the rate of chain initiation (5 sec−1) was far more rapid than with Cyclin E peptide and SCFFBW7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and Table 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and Table 3.

claim: When saturating levels (10 μM) of the ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBE2R2 was assayed with both SCFFBW7 and Cyclin E peptide or with SCFβTRCP with β-Catenin peptide, the rates of chain initiation were highly similar (0.1 sec−1–0.2 sec−1, respectively).
source: When saturating levels (10 μM) of the ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBE2R2 was assayed with both SCFFBW7 and Cyclin E peptide or with SCFβTRCP with β-Catenin peptide, the rates of chain initiation were highly similar (0.1 sec−1–0.2 sec−1, respectively) and comparable to the rates generated by ARIH1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4 and Table 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4 and Table 3.

claim: The rate of the second ubiquitin transfer by UBE2R2 was far more rapid for both substrates and SCF complexes (40 sec−1 and 30 sec−1 to mono-ubiquitylated Cyclin E and β-Catenin peptides, respectively).
source: Consistent with prior results, the rate of the second ubiquitin transfer was far more rapid for both substrates and SCF complexes (40 sec−1 and 30 sec−1 to mono-ubiquitylated Cyclin E and β-Catenin peptides, respectively).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4 and Table 3.

claim: Reduction of the UBE2R2 levels by 20-fold to mimic cellular conditions resulted in the near elimination of any product for both Cyclin E and β-Catenin peptide.
source: While reactions containing saturating UBE2R2 for SCF added impressively long poly-ubiquitin chains onto substrate, reduction of the UBE2R2 levels by 20-fold to mimic cellular conditions resulted in the near elimination of any product for both Cyclin E and β-Catenin peptide (Figure 2—figure supplement 5 and Table 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The stabilities of the SCFFBW7 substrates p27 and CYCLIN E were comparable by cycloheximide chase in either wild-type (WT) or UBE2R1 knock out HEK293T Flp-In T-Rex (293T-FiTx cells).
source: Surprisingly, the stabilities of the SCFFBW7 substrates p27 and CYCLIN E were comparable by cycloheximide chase in either wild-type (WT) or UBE2R1 knock out HEK293T Flp-In T-Rex (293T-FiTx cells; Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Ablation of UBE2R1 protein did not significantly affect UBE2R2 mRNA levels.
source: Note that ablation of UBE2R1 protein did not significantly affect UBE2R2 mRNA levels, ruling out a dosage compensation effect (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The steady state levels of three SCF substrates, β-CATENIN, CYCLIN E, and p27, were not significantly enriched in three independent UBE2R1/2 knockout cell lines in comparison with three control lines.
source: Remarkably, the steady state levels of three SCF substrates, β-CATENIN, CYCLIN E, and p27, were not significantly enriched in three independent UBE2R1/2 knockout cell lines in comparison with three control lines (Figure 5a,b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 5a,b.

claim: Cycloheximide chase analysis performed on the UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells demonstrated that p27 protein degradation was indistinguishable in comparison with control cells.
source: Cycloheximide chase analysis performed on the UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells demonstrated that p27 protein degradation was indistinguishable in comparison with control cells (Figure 5c and Figure 5—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The degradation of IκBα in response to TNFα treatment in control or UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells was indistinguishable.
source: The degradation of IκBα in response to TNFα treatment in control or UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells was also indistinguishable (Figure 5d and Figure 5—figure supplement 3b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Flow cytometry was used to estimate the percentage of cells in each phase of the cell cycle in control versus UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells but no differences were found.
source: Finally, since Cdc34 is required for the G1-S cell cycle transition in budding yeast, flow cytometry was used to estimate the percentage of cells in each phase of the cell cycle in control versus UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells but no differences were found (Figure 5e and Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 5e.

claim: Both UBE2R1 and UBE2R2 are entirely dispensable for the degradation of at least some SCF substrates and progression through the cell cycle.
source: These results demonstrated that both UBE2R1 and UBE2R2 are entirely dispensable for the degradation of at least some SCF substrates and progression through the cell cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens were performed in the NALM-6 pre-B cell lymphoma line with the previously reported EKO sgRNA library to identify genes that exhibit synthetic lethality with the loss of UBE2R1 and/or UBE2R2.
source: To address this question in an unbiased manner, we performed genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens in the NALM-6 pre-B cell lymphoma line with the previously reported EKO sgRNA library (Bertomeu et al., 2018) to identify genes that exhibit synthetic lethality with the loss of UBE2R1 and/or UBE2R2.
evidence: This describes a method used in the study, with results shown in Figure 6.

claim: The UBE2G1 gene scored as the top synthetic lethal interactor in both replicates of the UBE2R1/2 double knockout screen but did not score in either of the UBE2R1 or UBE2R2 single knockout screens.
source: Strikingly, the UBE2G1 gene scored as the top synthetic lethal interactor in both replicates of the UBE2R1/2 double knockout screen but did not score in either of the UBE2R1 or UBE2R2 single knockout screens (Figure 6b–e).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the CRISPR screen shown in Figure 6.

claim: Out of the five experimental screens analyzed, the only statistically significant hit (FDR < 0.05) was UBE2G1 in the UBE2R1/2 double knockout screen.
source: Moreover, out of the five experimental screens analyzed, the only statistically significant hit (FDR < 0.05) was UBE2G1 in the UBE2R1/2 double knockout screen.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the CRISPR screen analysis.

claim: p27 levels were modestly increased in populations treated with non-targeting siRNAs but were strongly increased in UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells treated with UBE2G1-targeting siRNA.
source: To determine whether depletion of UBE2G1 may affect the stability of SCF substrates, UBE2R1/2 double knockout 293T cell lines were treated with siRNAs targeting UBE2G1. p27 levels were modestly increased in populations treated with non-targeting siRNAs but were strongly increased in UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells treated with UBE2G1-targeting siRNA (Figure 7a,b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 7a,b.

claim: Stabilization of CYCLIN E protein was observed in UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells treated with UBE2G1-targeting siRNA.
source: Stabilization of CYCLIN E protein was also observed in UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells treated with UBE2G1-targeting siRNA.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 7a,b.

claim: HIF1α was heavily stabilized upon knockdown of UBE2G1 in UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells.
source: To determine whether these observations might extend to additional CRLs, we assessed the CRL2VHL substrate HIF1α in control versus UBE2R1/2 knockout cell lines. Similar to p27, HIF1α was heavily stabilized upon knockdown of UBE2G1 in UBE2R1/2 double knockout cells (Figure 7a,b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genetic experiments shown in Figure 7a,b.

claim: UBE2G1 itself had no measurable chain initiation activity, but exhibited substantial chain elongation activity against either mono-ubiquitylated β-Catenin or Cyclin E peptides in the presence of SCFFBW7 or SCFβTRCP, respectively.
source: We then determined whether UBE2G1 can support SCF-mediated substrate ubiquitylation in vitro. UBE2G1 itself had no measurable chain initiation activity, but exhibited substantial chain elongation activity against either mono-ubiquitylated β-Catenin or Cyclin E peptides in the presence of SCFFBW7 or SCFβTRCP, respectively (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the in vitro kinetic experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1a.

claim: The Km of UBE2G1 was estimated as 1.30 ± 0.2 μM from multi-turnover Michaelis-Menten kinetics in the presence of mono-ubiquitylated Cyclin E peptide substrate.
source: The Km of UBE2G1 was estimated as 1.30 ± 0.2 μM from multi-turnover Michaelis-Menten kinetics in the presence of mono-ubiquitylated Cyclin E peptide substrate (Figure 7—figure supplement 1b,c and Table 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b,c and Table 1.

claim: Maximal chain elongation on substrate was observed only when ARIH1 or UBE2D3 were assayed in the presence of UBE2G1.
source: We then tested the ability of UBE2G1 to participate in a hand-off reaction with either ARIH1 or UBE2D3. Maximal chain elongation on substrate was observed only when ARIH1 or UBE2D3 were assayed in the presence of UBE2G1 (Figure 7c,d).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the in vitro kinetic experiments shown in Figure 7c,d.

claim: The pre-steady state kinetics of UBE2G1-catalyzed ubiquitin transfer to the Cyclin E peptide yielded rates of ubiquitin transfer of 1 ± 0.1 sec−1 under conditions where UBE2G1 levels were sufficient to saturate SCF.
source: Finally, the pre-steady state kinetics of UBE2G1-catalyzed ubiquitin transfer to the Cyclin E peptide yielded rates of ubiquitin transfer of 1 ± 0.1 sec−1 under conditions where UBE2G1 levels were sufficient to saturate SCF (Figure 7e, Figure 7—figure supplement 1d, and Table 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinetic experiments shown in Figure 7e and Table 3.

claim: The UBE2R2 efficiency (1.3 × 108 M−1 sec−1) was 173-fold greater than for UBE2G1 (7.7 × 105 M−1 sec−1) for the first ubiquitin transfer to mono-ubiquitylated substrate.
source: In terms of enzyme efficiency (kobs/Km), the UBE2R2 efficiency (1.3 × 108 M−1 sec−1) was 173-fold greater than for UBE2G1 (7.7 × 105 M−1 sec−1) for the first ubiquitin transfer to mono-ubiquitylated substrate, and 17-fold greater for the subsequent transfer.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the kinetic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: UBE2G1 activity is sufficient to poly-ubiquitylate substrates that have been primed by either UBE2D1/2/3 or ARIH1.
source: Thus, while UBE2R2 is far more efficient during catalysis of ubiquitin transfer to substrate on SCF, UBE2G1 activity is nevertheless sufficient to poly-ubiquitylate substrates that have been primed by either UBE2D1/2/3 or ARIH1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic experiments.

claim: UBE2G1 can act as a dedicated elongation E2 for SCF complexes, and thereby buffer cells against the loss of UBE2R1 and UBE2R2.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrated that UBE2G1 can act as a dedicated elongation E2 for SCF complexes, and thereby buffer cells against the loss of UBE2R1 and UBE2R2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: Comparison of the ARIH1- or UBE2D3-catalyzed ubiquitin chain initiation demonstrates that the rates are not substantially affected by enzyme concentrations that range from physiological to saturating levels.
source: First, comparison of the ARIH1- or UBE2D3-catalyzed ubiquitin chain initiation demonstrates that the rates are not substantially affected by enzyme concentrations that range from physiological to saturating levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic experiments.

claim: While the rates of ubiquitin chain initiation by UBE2R2 when saturating for SCF are comparable to those of ARIH1 and UBE2D3, at physiological levels UBE2R2 clearly cannot support ubiquitin chain initiation or ubiquitylated product formation.
source: Second, while the rates of ubiquitin chain initiation by UBE2R2 when saturating for SCF are comparable to those of ARIH1 and UBE2D3, at physiological levels UBE2R2 clearly cannot support ubiquitin chain initiation or ubiquitylated product formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic experiments.

claim: The rate of chain initiation by UBE2D3 for β-Catenin peptide and SCFβTRCP is some 50-fold faster than for reactions containing SCFFBW7 and Cyclin E peptide, indicating that UBE2D3 has a strong preference for some substrates and/or substrate receptors.
source: Third, the rate of chain initiation by UBE2D3 for β-Catenin peptide and SCFβTRCP is some 50-fold faster than for reactions containing SCFFBW7 and Cyclin E peptide, indicating that UBE2D3 has a strong preference for some substrates and/or substrate receptors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic experiments.

claim: UBE2R1/2 function is genetically buffered by UBE2G1, such that loss of UBE2R1/2 does not cause overt proliferation defects in cell line models, whereas the simultaneous loss of all three E2s leads to inviability.
source: Finally, UBE2R1/2 function is genetically buffered by UBE2G1, such that loss of UBE2R1/2 does not cause overt proliferation defects in cell line models, whereas the simultaneous loss of all three E2s leads to inviability.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic experiments.

claim: Human SCF-catalyzed substrate ubiquitylation has evolved additional regulatory layers compared to the simpler yeast SCF system.
source: Our results suggest that human SCF-catalyzed substrate ubiquitylation has evolved additional regulatory layers compared to the simpler yeast SCF system (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, Cdc34 appears both necessary and sufficient for SCF function since Ubc4/5 (the UBE2D1/2/3 orthologs) have no in vitro activity with reconstituted yeast SCF and cannot compensate for the loss of CDC34 in cells.
source: In S. cerevisiae, Cdc34 appears both necessary and sufficient for SCF function since Ubc4/5 (the UBE2D1/2/3 orthologs) have no in vitro activity with reconstituted yeast SCF and cannot compensate for the loss of CDC34 in cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about yeast SCF function.

claim: The concentration of Cdc34 in the yeast nucleus has been estimated at approximately 10 μM and 2- to 3-fold lower in the cytoplasm.
source: The concentration of Cdc34 in the yeast nucleus has been estimated at approximately 10 μM and 2- to 3-fold lower in the cytoplasm (Kleiger et al., 2009a).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: UBE2R1/2 protein levels in several human cell lines are at least an order of magnitude lower than in yeast, and well-below the low micromolar value of the Km of UBE2R2 for SCF bound to an unmodified substrate.
source: In contrast, UBE2R1/2 protein levels in several human cell lines are at least an order of magnitude lower than in yeast, and well-below the low micromolar value of the Km of UBE2R2 for SCF bound to an unmodified substrate (Table 1).
evidence: This is a comparison of the data in Table 2 with prior research on yeast Cdc34 levels.

claim: The Km of UBE2R2 for SCF bound to a mono-ubiquitylated substrate is approximately 0.3 μM, similar to the physiological concentration of UBE2R1/2 in tissue culture cells.
source: On the other hand, the Km of UBE2R2 for SCF bound to a mono-ubiquitylated substrate is approximately 0.3 μM, similar to the physiological concentration of UBE2R1/2 in tissue culture cells, thus explaining why UBE2R1/2 is still able to promote chain elongation on primed substrate in vitro.
evidence: This is a comparison of the data in Table 1 and Table 2.

claim: A fraction of UBE2R1 is concentrated into foci in which protein levels may be higher.
source: A possible exception to this interpretation may be our observation that a fraction of UBE2R1 is concentrated into foci in which protein levels may be higher (Figure 5—figure supplement 5), and thus potentially capable of initiating localized ubiquitylation reactions with CRL ligases.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the immunofluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: Multiple E3s contain sequence motifs that may drive the formation of membraneless organelles such as nuclear speckles and Cajal bodies.
source: Multiple E3s contain sequence motifs that may drive the formation of membraneless organelles such as nuclear speckles and Cajal bodies (Hughes et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The CUL3 substrate receptor SPOP forms such structures in cells in the presence of its substrates.
source: In particular, the CUL3 substrate receptor SPOP forms such structures in cells in the presence of its substrates (Bouchard et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: CRL function is more buffered in human cells compared to yeast.
source: Our genome-wide genetic screen suggests that CRL function is more buffered in human cells compared to yeast.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CRISPR screen results.

claim: Aside from UBE2G1, at the level of resolution of our screen, we detected no other significant genetic interactions with loss of UBE2R1/2, including ARIH1 and UBE2D3.
source: Aside from UBE2G1, at least at the level of resolution of our screen, we detected no other significant genetic interactions with loss of UBE2R1/2, including ARIH1 and UBE2D3.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the CRISPR screen shown in Figure 6.

claim: The elongation activity of ARIH1 and UBE2D3 are insufficient to compensate for the combined loss of UBE2R1/2 and UBE2G1.
source: This result implies that the elongation activity of ARIH1 and UBE2D3 are insufficient to compensate for the combined loss of UBE2R1/2 and UBE2G1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CRISPR screen results.

claim: Conditional alleles of CDC34 exhibit many dozens of well-documented synthetic lethal interactions in yeast.
source: In contrast, conditional alleles of CDC34 exhibit many dozens of well-documented synthetic lethal interactions in yeast (Oughtred et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: While the UBE2R1/2 double mutant is viable in two different transformed cell lines, UBE2R1/2 function may still be essential or at least important in other cell lines.
source: We note that while the UBE2R1/2 double mutant is viable in two different transformed cell lines, UBE2R1/2 function may still be essential or at least important in other cell lines.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental results.

claim: The reduction of UBE2R1 protein levels in U2OS cells resulted in partial stabilization of IKBα.
source: For instance, the reduction of UBE2R1 protein levels in U2OS cells resulted in partial stabilization of IKBα (Wu et al., 2010) and UBE2R1/2 function may still be required in an organismal context, an issue that remains to be addressed.
